interest: This file illustrates the State Department's decimal filing and cross-referencing practices during the interwar and World War II eras, specifically demonstrating how comparative regional economic intelligence spanning both China and Japan was managed. It highlights wartime economic intelligence on the East Asian tea trade and the involvement of P. E. Witham, a British advisor serving Chinese Nationalist trade organizations during the Second Sino-Japanese War. For economic and diplomatic historians, it provides a crucial pointer to detailed comparative production and export data for 1937–1938 filed under the China decimal file (893.61332).
overview: This file (894.61332) consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' sheet dated October 12, 1945, which functions as a cross-reference docket sheet for records relating to the tea industry in Japan. The sole entry records Despatch No. 362 of January 6, 1939, from American Consul General Addison E. Southard in Hong Kong, transmitting a memorandum comparing the tea industries of China and Japan in 1937 and 1938 prepared by P. E. Witham, British technical advisor to the Chinese Foreign Trade Commission and the China National Tea Corporation. Because the primary subject was classified under China, the document was transferred and filed under decimal file 893.61332/1r, leaving this list of papers as the only record in this Japanese classification.

subfiles.summary: A Department of State 'List of Papers' sheet (Form 01-46, dated October 12, 1945) indexing papers under subject 894.61332 (Tea, Japan). The single entry records Hong Kong Despatch No. 362 of January 6, 1939, from Consul General Addison E. Southard, forwarding a memorandum comparing the Chinese and Japanese tea industries during 1937 and 1938. The memorandum was prepared by P. E. Witham, British technical advisor to both the Chinese Foreign Trade Commission and the China National Tea Corporation. A purport note indicates that the actual paper was cross-referenced and filed under the China internal affairs decimal file as 893.61332/1r.
